test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Where is a typical clutch operated by several coiled springs?

options.text: On the pitch circle near the periphery
On the addendum circle near the center of the radius
On the interval circle near the central axis of the shaft
On the base circle near the center of the circle

solution:
The correct answer is __On the pitch circle near the periphery.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Coiled springs__ in a typical clutch are designed to provide the necessary clamping force.
 
• These springs are generally positioned on the pitch circle near the periphery of the clutch.
 
• This arrangement ensures even pressure distribution on the clutch plate.
 
• The placement of the springs allows efficient transmission of torque from the engine to the drivetrain.
 
• It also helps in minimizing wear and tear on the clutch components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Clutch Components:**

 
 
• The clutch consists of the clutch plate, pressure plate, release bearing, and coiled springs.
 
• The coiled springs play a crucial role in maintaining the contact between the clutch plate and the flywheel.
 
 
 
• **Types of Clutches:**
 
 
• There are several types of clutches including single plate clutch, multi-plate clutch, and centrifugal clutch.
 
• Single plate clutches are commonly used in cars and light commercial vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Clutch Operation:**
 
 
• The clutch allows the driver to engage or disengage the engine from the drivetrain.
 
• This is essential for smooth gear changes and starting or stopping the vehicle.
